dedupe_keys.name: openstreetmap derived residential and non residential building classification for the united states

description: This dataset labels every OpenStreetMap building footprint in the United States as residential or non-residential, using the footprint geometry and the OpenStreetMap tags and points of interest around it. Files are one GeoPackage per county or equivalent, named by state-county code and grouped by core-based statistical area so they link to official statistics, and each building keeps the OpenStreetMap information used to classify it, so sheds and garages can be filtered out. The authors validated the labels against authoritative land use data for selected counties and report high precision for non-residential buildings and high recall for residential ones. Coverage: the whole United States, limited to buildings present in OpenStreetMap. Access: free on OSF, with code on GitHub. Licence: CC BY 4.0 on the OSF project. Caveats: coverage follows OpenStreetMap completeness; data are in UTM zones, so counties must be reprojected before merging, and buildings on county borders appear twice. Simulation uses are population allocation to buildings, residential exposure counts for hazard models and synthetic populations for agent-based evacuation and mobility models. Related records: OpenStreetMap, the Microsoft US building footprints and FEMA USA Structures.
